content: Flunisolide is a corticosteroid medication prescribed to prevent allergy symptoms such as sneezing, itching, and a runny or congested nose. It may also be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Flunisolide is available as a nasal inhalation solution. It is typically inhaled one to four times daily at evenly spaced intervals. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it or use it more frequently than prescribed. Do not stop using flunisolide without consulting your doctor. Before using it for the first time, read the written instructions provided with the medication. Ask your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist to demonstrate the correct technique, and practice using the inhaler in their presence. To use the nasal inhaler, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly. 2. Gently blow your nose to clear your nasal passages. 3. Remove the cap from the nasal inhaler. 4. Shake the inhaler well. 5. Prime the pump by aiming the nasal sprayer away from people and animals and pressing down until a fine spray appears. 6. Hold the spray bottle by placing two fingers on the shoulders of the bottle and your thumb on the bottom. Use your thumb to press the spray bottle firmly and quickly. 7. Insert the tip of the nasal inhaler about 1/4 inch into one nostril, pointing the tip toward the outer side of your nose. 8. Close your other nostril with your finger and tilt your head back slightly. 9. Press down on the container to release the medication while gently sniffing with your mouth closed. 10. Hold your breath for a few seconds. 11. Exhale through your mouth. 12. Remove the nasal inhaler from your nose. 13. Clean the tip of the nasal inhaler with a tissue and replace the cap. 14. Repeat steps 3 through 12 for the other nostril if directed by your doctor. 15. Wash your hands again. Avoid blowing your nose for 15 minutes after inhaling the prescribed dose. Before using flunisolide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to flunisolide or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), arthritis medications, aspirin, cyclosporine, digoxin, diuretics, estrogen, ketoconazole, oral contraceptives, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifampin, theophylline, and vitamins. If you have a nasal or fungal infection (other than on your skin), consult your doctor before using flunisolide. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had tuberculosis, liver, kidney, intestinal, or heart disease, diabetes, an underactive thyroid gland, high blood pressure, mental illness, myasthenia gravis, osteoporosis, herpes eye infection, seizures, or ulcers. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using flunisolide, contact your doctor. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one. Flunisolide may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: headache, nasal irritation or dryness, sore throat, sneezing, or nosebleeds. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: increased difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, lower legs, or ankles, vision problems, prolonged cold or infection, or muscle weakness. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store flunisolide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist about disposal methods. Avoid puncturing the aerosol container and do not discard it in an incinerator or fire. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Your symptoms may improve within a few days, but if they do not improve within three weeks, contact your doctor. Avoid exposure to chickenpox and measles, as this medication increases your susceptibility to these illnesses. If exposed, contact your doctor. Do not receive vaccinations or immunizations unless approved by your doctor. Report any injuries or signs of infection (e.g., fever, sore throat, pain during urination, or muscle aches) during treatment. If your sputum thickens or changes color (e.g., from clear white to yellow, green, or gray), contact your doctor, as this may indicate an infection. Regularly clean your inhalation device and replace it as needed, following the instructions provided with your inhaler. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist with any questions about refilling your prescription.
